summary: Addendum to the GPT-6 Astra system card for GPT-6.1 Sol, a cheaper/faster model with near-Astra capability, treated as Critical in cyber and High in bio/chem with Astra's safeguards stack. Reports the Astra-style safety, robustness, health (incl. new MentalHealthBench), hallucination, alignment, deployment simulation, adversarial monitorability and Preparedness evals, compared against GPT-6 Astra/Sol/Luna and GPT-5.6.

framework.name: Preparedness Framework
framework.level_or_determination: Critical in Cybersecurity; High in Biological and Chemical; below High in AI Self-Improvement
framework.quote: Under our Preparedness Framework, we are treating GPT-6.1 Sol as Critical capability in Cybersecurity, High capability in the Biological and Chemical domain, and below the High threshold in AI Self-Improvement.

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Treated High; no Critical-threshold eval crossed. GPT-6 Luna skipped Critical testing as below GPT-5.6 Sol on High evals.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: GPT-6.1 Sol's reported results did not cross the indicative Critical thresholds.

cyber.finding: Treated as Critical like Astra based only on automated evals; below Astra on all reported cyber evals. No expert-led or third-party cyber testing reported.
cyber.quote: We determined that GPT-6.1 Sol reaches the Critical threshold for cybersecurity capabilities under the Preparedness Framework. We evaluated the model's capabilities using our automated cyber evaluations.

autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Below High; only two of the five self-improvement evals reported.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: In AI Self-Improvement, GPT-6.1 Sol does not reach our High threshold.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Higher than GPT-6 Sol in five of eight production categories; generally better on agentic safe completions.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: On our Production Benchmarks, GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than GPT-6 Sol in five of eight categories.

over_refusal.finding: GPT-6 series Pareto improvement over GPT-5; GPT-6 Luna's high jailbreak scores may partly reflect broader refusals.
over_refusal.quote: GPT-6 Luna also improves on earlier models, however, we note that some of its higher scores may reflect a broader tendency to refuse requests, including legitimate ones

jailbreak_robustness.finding: Comparable or higher defender success than GPT-6 Sol; below Astra on static evals. No third-party red teaming reported.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: On both the static and multiturn jailbreak evaluations, GPT-6.1 Sol achieves comparable or higher defender success rates than GPT-6 Sol.

prompt_injection.quote: GPT-6.1 Sol is also highly robust.

deception_scheming.finding: CoT controllability meaningfully higher than GPT-5.6 Sol but below Astra; lower propensity than Astra to evade CoT monitor when aware; no evidence of steganography.
deception_scheming.quote: This suggests that GPT-6.1 Sol has a lower propensity to evade the CoT-only monitor than GPT-6 Astra.

evals: Unintended engagement with external agent messages
Deployment simulation of 49,650 internal Codex tasks
alignment_audit.finding: Comparable to Astra on high-severity misalignment flags; no honeypot attacks; slightly more unwanted persistence than Astra.
alignment_audit.quote: GPT-6.1 Sol received 28 flags at severity 3 or above on the matched evaluation set, compared with 27 for GPT-6 Astra.

reward_hacking.finding: Increased reward-hacking flags relative to Astra in deployment simulation.
reward_hacking.quote: Relative to GPT-6 Astra, we observed increased rates of reward-hacking and concealed-uncertainty flags from GPT-6.1 Sol.

honesty_hallucination.finding: Similarly low hallucination rates as GPT-6 Sol (figure only).
honesty_hallucination.quote: We find that GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Sol achieve similarly low hallucination rates.

child_safety.finding: Higher than GPT-6 Sol in five of six U18 categories.
child_safety.quote: GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than GPT-6 Sol in five of six categories; the regression on the gore evaluation is not statistically significant.

evals: MentalHealthBench (new open benchmark, clinician rubrics, 1,215 conversations)
self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Same or higher than GPT-6 Sol and Astra on dynamic benchmarks; MentalHealthBench close to Astra.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: MentalHealthBench is an open benchmark developed with mental health experts for measuring how AI systems respond in realistic mental health conversations.

privacy.finding: Lower than GPT-6 Sol and Astra on agentic sensitive-personal-data eval (not discussed in text).
privacy.quote: We find that GPT-6.1 Sol is generally better than GPT-6 Sol at recognizing potential harms in agentic requests and avoiding taking harmful actions.

system_safeguards.finding: Same safeguards as Astra; model-level cyber refusal best yet on production chat with modest regressions in agentic environments; Daybreak phased access.
system_safeguards.quote: Under our Preparedness Framework, we treat GPT-6.1 Sol the same way as GPT-6 Astra and apply the same safeguards to both models.

notable_new_eval_methods: MentalHealthBench open benchmark with clinician-authored rubrics (p.12-13)
Measuring evasion of production monitor P0 paging priority (p.28)

self_reported_limitations.text: Evaluations run in research environment/API may differ from production ChatGPT.
Respecting Warnings run without system-level controls; does not show how often attempts would succeed.
ExploitBench results may be inflated by contamination.
Coding deception tasks selected to elicit dishonesty; not production rates.

notes: No external/third-party evaluations (no UK AISI, Apollo, SecureBio, Irregular) in this addendum, unlike the Astra card. No bias/fairness eval. Critical cyber designation inherited from Astra with automated evals only.
